title: Modernising Retail at Scale: Architecting a Cloud‑to‑Edge Platform for a Global Enterprise
gist: Tesco Senior Engineering Director Jayesh Bhayani recounts a decade-long shift from siloed, outsourced legacy stacks to a single insourced multi-tenant retail platform spanning private cloud, public cloud and offline-capable store edge, stressing cost discipline (public cloud is ~20% of footprint but ~80% of cost), portable PaaS to avoid lock-in, and that agentic commerce via ChatGPT/Gemini-style agents is a business decision that risks disintermediating retailers while protocols like ACP and UCP are not production-ready.

themes.theme: Tesco scale and legacy starting point

insights.claim: Tesco operates about 5,000 stores in five countries, 20 distribution centers, 25 million customers, 350,000 colleagues (about 6,000 in technology), around 50 million baskets and 1.3 million online orders a week, almost 50,000 POS tills, and 4.5 billion calls a day.
insights.speaker: Jayesh Bhayani
insights.so_what: Sets the scale context for Tesco's technology spend and the mission-criticality of its in-house platform.
insights.locator: First of all, some context into how large Tesco is.

insights.claim: During COVID Tesco doubled its online delivery slots within a month, which Bhayani equates to putting almost three competitor companies online, while many rivals stopped taking orders or signing customers.
insights.speaker: Jayesh Bhayani
insights.so_what: Evidence that a pre-built scalable e-commerce platform became a competitive advantage in a demand shock.
insights.locator: When COVID happened, when entire business shifted towards online

insights.claim: A decade ago Tesco ran siloed stacks (.NET, Oracle) per business with no single customer login, no single source of truth for stock or pricing, 20-year-old batch POS software deployed by floppy disk, servers taking two months to provision, and heavily customized vendor software that locked it in and took six to nine months for minor POS changes.
insights.speaker: Jayesh Bhayani
insights.so_what: Illustrates how customization of vendor software at scale creates long-term lock-in, a caution for enterprise software buyers.
insights.locator: No single source of truth for stock or pricing.

insights.claim: Tesco's entire UK and Republic of Ireland business now runs 100% on its single multi-tenant retail platform, with rollout progressing into Central European markets.
insights.speaker: Jayesh Bhayani
insights.so_what: Completion of platform consolidation enables reuse across markets and faster delivery.
insights.locator: Where are we now?

insights.claim: Bhayani argues enterprise transformation requires three simultaneous pillars, system, talent and process transformation, and that system modernization alone fails without insourcing talent, redefining career paths and replacing program-led delivery with product-driven agile teams.
insights.speaker: Jayesh Bhayani
insights.so_what: Large-enterprise modernizations that only buy technology tend to underdeliver; watch for org change as the leading indicator.
insights.locator: Ecosystem of Transformation

insights.claim: To insource development, Tesco added engineering hubs in Hungary and Poland alongside the UK and India, created a product management function that previously did not exist, and aligned its technology org to its four business units (supply chain and distribution, commercial, channels, customer).
insights.speaker: Jayesh Bhayani
insights.so_what: Shift from outsourced consultants to insourced talent reduces revenue for IT outsourcing firms serving large retailers.
insights.locator: Back then we were only across two different locations

insights.claim: Tesco follows a 'build and buy' rule: build what is a core differentiator (its retail platform, homegrown POS on every till, scan-as-you-shop handhelds, cameras) and buy non-differentiating back-office systems such as HR and finance, with platform integration mandatory for bought tools.
insights.speaker: Jayesh Bhayani
insights.so_what: Large retailers are building rather than buying POS and commerce platforms, limiting the addressable market for retail-software vendors at the top end.
insights.locator: One of the very early things we had to decide was build and buy.

insights.claim: Tesco replaced centralized change-control and architecture review boards with decentralized teams operating under clear domain boundaries and standards ('freedom within the guardrail'), which Bhayani says is even more necessary with an agentic workforce arriving.
insights.speaker: Jayesh Bhayani
insights.so_what: Governance via guardrails rather than gates is the operating model enterprises are adopting for AI-assisted development.
insights.locator: Now, centralization versus decentralization.

insights.claim: Transformation at a 100-year-old company cannot be big bang; Tesco sequenced small changes where business and customer demand existed to build trust, after which business demand for technology grew with fewer questions.
insights.speaker: Jayesh Bhayani
insights.so_what: Incremental modernization is the realistic path for incumbents; watch for trust-building wins before large platform bets.
insights.locator: The sequence is very important.

insights.claim: Grocery is a roughly 3-4.5% margin business, so Tesco treats cost as a feature rather than a constraint; four to five years ago its public cloud spend exceeded £50-60 million and was growing exponentially, which on a £50 billion business with ~£2 billion margin materially hits P&L.
insights.speaker: Jayesh Bhayani
insights.so_what: Low-margin enterprises are price-sensitive cloud customers prone to optimization and repatriation, a headwind for hyperscaler growth in such verticals.
insights.quote: cost is a feature for us, not a constraint.
insights.locator: Offline operations.

insights.claim: About 80% of Tesco's compute presence is in private cloud and 20% in public cloud, but the cost split is the exact reverse, with an equivalent setup costing almost 8 to 10 times more in public cloud.
insights.speaker: Jayesh Bhayani
insights.so_what: A large-enterprise data point supporting the hybrid/private cloud repatriation thesis and the cost premium of public cloud.
insights.quote: It costs almost 8 to 10 times more for an equivalent setup in public cloud.
insights.locator: It's almost 80-20, 80% of our presence is in private cloud

insights.claim: Tesco initially handed developers credit cards to sign up for public cloud, producing large unattributed costs and forcing repatriation and re-migration; Bhayani says building centralized capabilities first would have avoided costly migrations.
insights.speaker: Jayesh Bhayani
insights.so_what: Uncontrolled early cloud adoption leads to later repatriation, a recurring pattern behind enterprise cloud-spend corrections.
insights.locator: We literally handed out credit cards

insights.claim: Tesco views public-cloud PaaS as a double-edged sword: proprietary PaaS creates lock-in and escalating license fees, but pure compute defeats the purpose of public cloud, so it uses portable PaaS technologies and reserves public cloud for workloads needing elasticity and customer proximity while running supply chain and distribution systems in private cloud.
insights.speaker: Jayesh Bhayani
insights.so_what: Large buyers actively resist proprietary hyperscaler services, favoring open/portable tech and limiting high-margin PaaS uptake.
insights.quote: If you are locked in, it's a very well-known fact that you will be held hostage.
insights.locator: If you are locked in

insights.claim: Bhayani warns that agentic code development today resembles public cloud ten years ago: a developer could spend almost £500 a day on AI tooling without clarity on the value created.
insights.speaker: Jayesh Bhayani
insights.so_what: Expect enterprise FinOps-style scrutiny and budget controls on AI coding spend, which could slow usage-based AI tooling revenue growth.
insights.quote: a developer could spend almost £500 a day without realizing or without clarity on what value is getting created
insights.locator: This is where as we are talking about agentic code development

insights.claim: Tesco protects against IP leakage from agentic code development and demands data-sharing and IP protections in SaaS contracts to preserve differentiation and avoid vendor lock-in.
insights.speaker: Jayesh Bhayani
insights.so_what: Enterprise data/IP terms are a gating factor for AI and SaaS vendor adoption.
insights.locator: We talked about the cost, IP and vendor lock-in.

insights.claim: Tesco runs the same microservices from its cloud on store edge devices so stores can operate offline, identifying club card loyalty and accepting card and contactless payments without network, and deliberately failing in the customer's favor, because replacing networks across the estate could cost hundreds of millions in a low-margin business.
insights.speaker: Jayesh Bhayani
insights.so_what: Edge-capable architecture is cheaper than network upgrades for large physical retailers, relevant for edge computing and electronic shelf label vendors.
insights.locator: Then comes the edge part of it.

insights.claim: Adding an item to a Tesco shopping cart calls at least 40 microservices (identity, product, customer UUID, personalization, price, description), so abstractions that avoid 40 network round trips from mobile to cloud are a performance necessity across 60-plus domains and hundreds of microservices.
insights.speaker: Jayesh Bhayani
insights.so_what: Shows latency/complexity costs of microservice architectures at retail scale.
insights.locator: For example, add an item to your shopping cart

insights.claim: Tesco keeps the same team responsible for both the edge and cloud retail platforms, and had teams own legacy systems during migration, because splitting new-build and legacy ownership destroys motivation and consistency.
insights.speaker: Jayesh Bhayani
insights.so_what: Ownership model lesson for large migrations.
insights.locator: In fact, when we were migrating from legacy stack

insights.claim: Because Tesco engineers own production support with no separate QA or support team, self-managing infrastructure such as Cassandra and Kafka became onerous, leading Tesco to invest heavily in centralized shared services; Bhayani's biggest regret is not building a central tech platform early, ending up with many duplicate CI/CD pipelines.
insights.speaker: Jayesh Bhayani
insights.so_what: Supports demand for internal developer platforms and managed data infrastructure in large enterprises.
insights.quote: I don't need 50 CI/CD pipelines, I need one CI/CD pipeline.
insights.locator: What could have been better?

insights.claim: Bhayani frames agentic commerce as a business decision with risk either way: retailers absent from AI agents like ChatGPT and Gemini can be marginalized, but participating also risks marginalization by ceding the first customer touchpoint to the agent platform.
insights.speaker: Jayesh Bhayani
insights.so_what: AI assistants threaten to disintermediate grocers' customer relationships, shifting bargaining power to AI platform owners.
insights.quote: If you don't go there, you can be marginalized. If you go there, you can still be marginalized because you're losing the first touch, customer experience.
insights.locator: Because that changes the paradigm completely.

insights.claim: Preparing for agentic commerce requires machine-readable data for agentic crawlers (AEO replacing SEO/SEM), agent gateways with identity, consent and policy controls, agent-to-agent protocols and MCP for discovery, turning the retail platform from a system of record into a system of delegation.
insights.speaker: Jayesh Bhayani
insights.so_what: New spend categories emerge around agent gateways, AEO and agent identity/consent infrastructure.
insights.quote: The platform completely evolves from a system of record, that's how it used to be, to a system of delegation.
insights.locator: Now the agentic crawlers will come

insights.claim: Tesco, in direct conversation on agentic commerce protocols UCP and ACP, says they are not ready for production at Tesco scale despite the marketing, and UK regulation currently does not allow agents to make payments on behalf of customers.
insights.speaker: Jayesh Bhayani
insights.so_what: Agentic commerce revenue at large grocers is likely further out than hype suggests; regulation is a gating factor in the UK.
insights.quote: As much as there is marketing, they are not ready.
insights.locator: The commerce protocol, ACP and UCP

insights.claim: Tesco has long used AI across supply chain forecasting (balancing lead times from multiple daily tomato deliveries to six-month lead times for jeans against shelf life), waste reduction, truck routing, ranging, personalization and pricing.
insights.speaker: Jayesh Bhayani
insights.so_what: Operational AI is mature at large grocers; incremental value now lies in agentic channels.
insights.locator: We have been using AI for a very long time at Tesco.
